question.text: Under PMLA Rules, when identifying the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) of an investor that is structured as a company investing in an AIF, what controlling-ownership-interest threshold applies?

answer.text: 25% controlling ownership interest for companies/trusts; 15% for partnership firms/unincorporated associations
5% controlling ownership interest for all investor types

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the PMLA (Maintenance of Records) Rules, UBO identification uses a 25% controlling ownership interest threshold for company and trust investors, and a 15% ownership or entitlement threshold for partnership firms and unincorporated associations of individuals. The AIF must trace back to the natural person(s) who ultimately own or control the investing institution. The Trap: Option A applies a 10% threshold that is not the PMLA UBO threshold. Options C and D use uniform 50% or 5% thresholds that do not match the PMLA Rules, which deliberately differentiate between corporate/trust investors and partnership/unincorporated associations. Note: Remember the split: 25% for companies and trusts, 15% for partnership firms and unincorporated associations of individuals; both thresholds are about controlling ownership interest used to identify the natural-person UBO.
